Liège Around Liège

Liège 84

Carré · Outremeuse · Batte · Montagne de Bueren · Guillemins · Palais · Curtius · Boverie

  1. Must see · Michelin & Fine Dining · Liège

    ¡Toma!

    One Michelin star — creative South-American-inspired cooking on the Sauvenière, one of the city's two starred tables in the 2026 guide.

    Boulevard de la Sauvenière 70, 4000 Liège, Belgium

    Recommended by Infolux, Foodle, Gault&millau, Ericboschman, Moustique

  2. Must see · Beer & Breweries · Liège

    Le Pot au Lait

    The Carré's mythic, wildly decorated bar — #8 in The European Bar Guide's Top 100 of 2025; big beer list, often-free gigs, open till 4am.

    Rue Sœurs-de-Hasque 9, 4000 Liège, Belgium

    Recommended by Paris Match Belgique, La Libre Belgique, Europeanbarguide, Culturetrip, RTBF (Belgian public broadcaster)

  3. Must see · French & Brasserie · Liège

    As Ouhès

    The busiest of the Place du Marché café-restaurants (the name is Walloon for 'the birds') — generous Walloon specialities like rabbit stewed in beer and big boulets on a terrace facing the Perron.

    Place du Marché 21, 4000 Liège, Belgium

    Recommended by Lonely Planet (FR edition), Uliege, Boulettes, Moustique, Visitliege

  4. Must see · Belgian & Flemish · Liège

    Café Lequet

    One of Liège's oldest cafés and the locals' answer to 'where for boulets?' — boulet-frites in sauce lapin is the house institution; a past Diamond Boulet winner of the Gay Boulet brotherhood.

    Quai sur Meuse 17, 4000 Liège, Belgium

    Recommended by Uliege, SNCB, Lonely Planet (FR edition), Boulettes

  5. Must see · Chocolate, Waffles & Sweets · Liège

    Une Gaufrette Saperlipopette

    Artisan waffle shop in the Mineurs quarter since 2010, making traditional pearl-sugar Liège waffles with good butter and eggs; also a house range of ice creams.

    Rue des Mineurs 6, 4000 Liège, Belgium

    Recommended by The Brussels Times (Hidden Belgium), RTBF (Belgian public broadcaster), Culturetrip, WBT

  6. Must see · Michelin & Fine Dining · Liège

    Héliport Brasserie

    One Michelin star — a 'brasserie gastronomique' set, per Michelin, in a pretty little castle some 10 km outside the centre (address Allée des Érables), all old beams and a summer terrace; creative French cooking.

    Allée des Érables, 4000 Liège, Belgium

    Recommended by Michelin, Infolux, Gault&millau, Ericboschman

  7. Must see · Michelin & Fine Dining · Liège

    Le Bistrot d'en Face

    Michelin Bib Gourmand bistro behind the Goffe market hall — a lyonnais-style room serving generous Liège and French bistro classics.

    Rue de la Goffe 8, 4000 Liège, Belgium

    Recommended by Michelin, Lavenir, Lonely Planet (FR edition), Gault&millau

  8. Must see · Beer & Breweries · Liège

    Brasserie C

    Liège's own city microbrewery since 2012, tucked at the foot of the Montagne de Bueren — brews Curtius (the city's blonde), Black {C} and Smash {C}; tours and tasting workshops, taproom Thu–Sun.

    Impasse des Ursulines 14, 4000 Liège, Belgium

    Recommended by Visitliege, RTBF (Belgian public broadcaster), SNCB, Moustique

  9. Must see · Liège

    Grand Curtius

    The early-17th-c. red-brick mansion of the arms merchant Jean Curtius on the Meuse, reopened in 2009 as one museum merging archaeology, weaponry, glass, decorative arts and Mosan religious art over 5,000 m².

    Quai de Maastricht 13, 4000 Liège, Belgium

    Recommended by Wikipedia, Visitliege, Official Site

  10. Must see · Liège

    Palais des Princes-Évêques

    The 16th-c. palace of the Prince-Bishops who ruled Liège for eight centuries, dominating Place Saint-Lambert; today the Palais de Justice, its arcaded first courtyard is open to walk through.

    Place Saint-Lambert, 4000 Liège, Belgium

    Recommended by Lonely Planet (FR edition), Le Guide du Routard (FR travel guide of record), Visitliege

  11. Must see · Liège

    Montagne de Bueren

    The 374-step stairway (1881) cut straight up the hillside from Hors-Château to the Citadelle, built so soldiers could reach town without the alleys — Liège's emblem and its best free climb, with a panorama over the roofs and the Meuse.

    Montagne de Bueren, 4000 Liège, Belgium

    Recommended by Visitliege, Lonely Planet (FR edition), Le Guide du Routard (FR travel guide of record)

  12. Must see · Liège

    La Boverie

    The city's fine-arts museum in a 1905 Exhibition palace on the Boverie island park, with a glass extension for blockbuster shows run in partnership with the Louvre; Ingres, Monet, Picasso and the Walloon school.

    Parc de la Boverie 3, 4020 Liège, Belgium

    Recommended by Lonely Planet (FR edition), Wikipedia, Liegecity

  13. Must see · Liège

    Cathédrale Saint-Paul et son Trésor

    Gothic cathedral since 1802 (after the revolutionaries razed Saint-Lambert); its Trésor holds the reliquary bust of Saint Lambert and the gold reliquary Charles the Bold gave in penance for sacking the city.

    Place de la Cathédrale, 4000 Liège, Belgium

    Recommended by Visitliege, Lonely Planet (FR edition), LA DH

  14. Must see · Liège

    Église Saint-Jacques

    Former Benedictine abbey church with a flamboyant-Gothic nave under a dazzling painted star vault, a Romanesque westwork and a Renaissance portal — Liège's most beautiful interior.

    Place Saint-Jacques, 4000 Liège, Belgium

    Recommended by Wikipedia, Visitliege, Lonely Planet (FR edition)

  15. Must see · Liège

    Place du Marché & le Perron

    The old market square in front of the 18th-c. town hall 'La Violette', ringed by café terraces; the Perron fountain at its centre is the symbol of Liège's civic liberties since the Middle Ages.

    Place du Marché, 4000 Liège, Belgium

    Recommended by Le Guide du Routard (FR travel guide of record), Visitliege, Awap

  16. Must see · Liège

    Marché de la Batte

    Every Sunday morning since 1561: Belgium's oldest and biggest street market stretches 2 km along the Meuse quays — fruit, Herve cheese, live poultry, flowers, books, and péket and gaufres to keep you going.

    Quai de la Batte, 4000 Liège, Belgium

    Recommended by Paris Match Belgique, RTBF (Belgian public broadcaster), LA DH

  17. Must see · French & Brasserie · Liège

    La Maison du Péket

    The péket temple in restored 18th-c. houses off Place du Marché — dozens of flavoured jenevers by the glass, and in its Amon Nanesse restaurant Liège dishes cooked with péket; the boulets here were filmed for Darley Newman's PBS travel series.

    Rue de l'Épée 2, 4000 Liège, Belgium

    Recommended by WBT, Darley Newman — Travels with Darley (PBS), Culturetrip

  18. Must see · French & Brasserie · Liège

    Tchantchès et Nanesse

    Outremeuse taverne named for the city's puppet hero and his wife — terroir cooking, boulets in sauce lapin and the folklore of the 'free republic' quarter.

    Rue Grande-Bêche 35, 4020 Liège, Belgium

    Recommended by WBT, Uliege, Moustique

  19. Must see · Beer & Breweries · Liège

    Le Petit Bougnat

    Outremeuse institution in the heart of Roture — terrace across the square in summer, all-night French-song sing-alongs in winter; the tourist office calls it essential.

    Rue Roture 17, 4020 Liège, Belgium

    Recommended by Visitliege, RTBF (Belgian public broadcaster), Lavenir

  20. Must see · Liège

    Collégiale Saint-Barthélemy

    Romanesque collegiate church with a twin-towered westwork, home to Renier de Huy's baptismal font (c. 1107–1118) — a lost-wax brass basin on ten oxen, a masterpiece of Mosan art.

    Place Saint-Barthélemy, 4000 Liège, Belgium

    Recommended by Le Guide du Routard (FR travel guide of record), WBT

  21. Must see · Liège

    Gare de Liège-Guillemins

    Santiago Calatrava's white steel-and-glass vault (2009) — a station with no façade, just a 160 m canopy over the tracks; worth the detour even if you arrive by car.

    Place des Guillemins 2, 4000 Liège, Belgium

    Recommended by Wikipedia, SNCB

  22. Must see · Liège

    Archéoforum

    Under Place Saint-Lambert: the excavated foundations of the vanished Cathedral of Saint-Lambert (razed 1794), a Gallo-Roman villa and finds back to the Mesolithic — the city's birthplace, walked underground.

    Place Saint-Lambert, 4000 Liège, Belgium

    Recommended by Wikipedia, Museumde

  23. Must see · Liège

    Coteaux de la Citadelle

    86 ha of terraced hillside orchards, vineyards, stairways and alleys between Hors-Château and the Citadelle — Liège's green lung, laureate of the Council of Europe Landscape Award; walk the Terrasses des Minimes for the views.

    Coteaux de la Citadelle, 4000 Liège, Belgium

    Recommended by Visitliege, Coe

  24. Must see · Liège

    Le Carré

    Liège's famous pedestrian nightlife block between the Boulevard de la Sauvenière and Pont d'Avroy — some thirty bars in four little streets, packed with students and the whole city at weekends, with no fixed closing time.

    Le Carré, 4000 Liège, Belgium

    Recommended by Visitliege, Culturetrip

  25. Must see · Michelin & Fine Dining · Liège

    Merry

    Gault&Millau-listed neo-gastronomic table on Rue des Carmes — bold, precise cooking that follows the seasons.

    Rue des Carmes 15, 4000 Liège, Belgium

    Recommended by Gault&millau, Moustique

  26. Must see · Michelin & Fine Dining · Liège

    Pépin

    Gault&Millau's 2026 Walloon H!P (hip & trendy) winner — concept, atmosphere and quality on the Esplanade Simone Veil.

    Esplanade Simone Veil 2, 4000 Liège, Belgium

    Recommended by Gault&millau, Paris Match Belgique

  27. Must see · French & Brasserie · Liège

    Le Dernier Ragot

    Two-time Diamond Boulet winner of the Confrérie du Gay Boulet (2005, 2006) — classic boulets in sauce lapin with proper frites, near the Carré.

    Rue des Clarisses 12, 4000 Liège, Belgium

    Recommended by Moustique, Wikipedia

  28. Must see · French & Brasserie · Liège

    Côté Cour Côté Jardin

    Warm, all-homemade Outremeuse brasserie whose boulets won the Confrérie du Gay Boulet's Boulet de Cristal in 2021; also good vegetarian dishes.

    Boulevard de la Constitution 48, 4020 Liège, Belgium

    Recommended by RTBF (Belgian public broadcaster), Moustique

  29. Must see · Michelin & Fine Dining · Liège

    Magma

    Michelin Bib Gourmand (2024) in Outremeuse — chef Tom Foguenne's farm-to-table cooking from local organic producers with a natural-wine list; one of two Liège Bibs announced in 2024.

    Rue Porte aux Oies 43, 4020 Liège, Belgium

    Recommended by Michelin, RTBF (Belgian public broadcaster)

  30. Worth the detour · Michelin & Fine Dining · Liège

    Sébastian

    Michelin Bib Gourmand since 2025 — farm-to-table, creative French cooking in the Carré near the cathedral.

    Rue de la Cathédrale 25, 4000 Liège, Belgium

    Recommended by Michelin, Paris Match Belgique, Gault&millau, Ericboschman

  31. Worth the detour · Beer & Breweries · Liège

    Les Brasseries de Liège (Légia)

    The brewers of Légia — the beer named for the river that gave Liège its name — born at Brasse & Vous in Rocourt and now brewing on the Quai sur Meuse.

    Quai sur Meuse 19, 4000 Liège, Belgium

    Recommended by Visitliege, RTBF (Belgian public broadcaster), Lavenir, Moustique

  32. Worth the detour · Liège

    Musée de la Vie wallonne

    The Province's folk-life museum in the 17th-c. Friars Minor convent — a century of Walloon everyday life, crafts, dialect and the Liège puppets (with marionnette shows).

    Cour des Mineurs, 4000 Liège, Belgium

    Recommended by Lonely Planet (FR edition), ERIH, Provinceliege

  33. Worth the detour · Liège

    Musée Tchantchès

    Museum of the 'Free Republic of Outremeuse' devoted to Tchantchès, Liège's cheeky wooden-puppet hero — his costumes, the Bisscheroux marionettes and puppet shows in season.

    Rue Surlet 56, 4020 Liège, Belgium

    Recommended by Visitliege, Museumde, LA DH

  34. Worth the detour · Liège

    Musée d'Ansembourg

    An 18th-c. merchant-banker's mansion on Féronstrée kept as a period house museum — Liège furniture, Cordoba leather wall-hangings, tapestries and stucco ceilings of the prince-bishops' golden age.

    En Féronstrée, 4000 Liège, Belgium

    Recommended by Wikipedia, Lonely Planet (FR edition), Awap

  35. Worth the detour · Liège

    Maison de la Métallurgie et de l'Industrie de Liège

    Industrial-heritage museum in the old Espérance-Longdoz steelworks — a working 17th-c.-style forge, blast-furnace models and the story of the coal and steel that made Liège.

    Boulevard Raymond Poincaré 17, 4020 Liège, Belgium

    Recommended by ERIH, Visitliege, RTBF (Belgian public broadcaster)

  36. Worth the detour · Liège

    Collégiale Saint-Jean-l'Évangéliste

    Founded c. 980 by Notger, Liège's first prince-bishop, who is buried here; an 11th-c. west tower fronts the 18th-c. rotunda church, and the cloister walls are lined with canons' tombstones — freshly restored.

    Quartier de l'Île, 4000 Liège, Belgium

    Recommended by Wikipedia, Visitliege, RTBF (Belgian public broadcaster)

  37. Worth the detour · Liège

    Théâtre de Liège (Émulation)

    Liège's main playhouse in the neoclassical Société libre d'Émulation building (Julien Koenig, 1934–39; the 1779 society's first hall was burned in the 1914 reprisals) — classified 1998, rebuilt by Pierre Hebbelinck & Pierre de Wit and reopened Oct 2013 with a 557-seat hall, bar and the Baci restaurant.

    Place du Vingt-Août 16, 4000 Liège, Belgium

    Recommended by Visitliege, La Libre Belgique, Lavenir

  38. Worth the detour · Michelin & Fine Dining · Liège

    La Cuisine de Yannick

    Michelin Bib Gourmand on Féronstrée, the museum street — a short seasonal set menu at a keen price.

    En Féronstrée 111, 4000 Liège, Belgium

    Recommended by Michelin, Moustique, Ericboschman

  39. Worth the detour · Beer & Breweries · Liège

    Brasserie de Jupille (Jupiler)

    Birthplace of Jupiler, Belgium's best-selling pils — AB InBev's giant Meuse-side brewery in Jupille, visitable by reservation (breweryvisits.com).

    Rue des Anciennes Houblonnières 2, 4020 Jupille (Liège), Belgium

    Recommended by LA DH, La Libre Belgique, Infolux

  40. Worth the detour · Michelin & Fine Dining · Liège

    Enoteca

    Michelin Bib Gourmand Italian enoteca on Rue de la Casquette in the centre; also a Culture Trip lunch pick.

    Rue de la Casquette 5, 4000 Liège, Belgium

    Recommended by Michelin, Culturetrip, Gault&millau

  41. Worth the detour · French & Brasserie · Liège

    Le Verre Bouteille

    Wine bar on the pedestrian Rue de la Casquette, one of the tourist office's picks for an apéritif and a Culture Trip best bar of Liège.

    Rue de la Casquette 13, 4000 Liège, Belgium

    Recommended by Visitliege, Culturetrip, RTBF (Belgian public broadcaster)

  42. Worth the detour · Café & Brown Café · Liège

    Grand Maison

    Fashionable brunch-and-lunch address on the Goffe quay — simple healthy plates and a big terrace looking over the Meuse.

    Quai de la Goffe 37, 4000 Liège, Belgium

    Recommended by RTBF (Belgian public broadcaster), Culturetrip, Moustique

  43. Worth the detour · Beer & Breweries · Liège

    La Grand Poste

    Liège's former central post office on the Meuse, reopened in Sept 2023 after four years' renovation as Liège's first food market — seven independent counters, a bar pouring beers brewed on site, coworking and the ULiège journalism campus upstairs.

    Quai sur Meuse 19, 4000 Liège, Belgium

    Recommended by Elle Belgique (lifestyle/food editorial), The Brussels Times (Hidden Belgium), RTBF (Belgian public broadcaster)

  44. Worth the detour · Liège

    La Cité Miroir

    The 1930s Sauvenière swimming baths, an Art Deco modernist landmark, reborn as a civic culture centre with exhibitions on memory and citizenship (incl. the permanent 'Plus jamais ça!' Holocaust route).

    Place Xavier Neujean 22, 4000 Liège, Belgium

    Recommended by SNCB, Visitliege

  45. Worth the detour · Liège

    Opéra royal de Wallonie

    The 1820 neoclassical Théâtre royal, Wallonia's opera house, with a modern rooftop extension; Grétry's heart is in an urn at the foot of his statue outside.

    Place de l'Opéra, 4000 Liège, Belgium

    Recommended by Wikipedia, Visitliege

  46. Worth the detour · Liège

    Aquarium-Muséum

    The University of Liège's aquarium (2,500 fish in some 50 tanks) and zoological museum in the 19th-c. Institut de Zoologie on the Meuse — a whale skeleton, dioramas and a cabinet of curiosities.

    Quai Édouard Van Beneden 22, 4020 Liège, Belgium

    Recommended by WBT, Lonely Planet (FR edition)

  47. Worth the detour · Liège

    Collégiale Saint-Denis

    One of Liège's seven collegiate churches (founded c. 987) with a fortress-like Romanesque tower; inside, a carved Brabant altarpiece of the Passion of St Denis (early 16th c.).

    Place Saint-Denis, 4000 Liège, Belgium

    Recommended by Le Guide du Routard (FR travel guide of record), Awap

  48. Worth the detour · Liège

    Mémorial interallié de Cointe

    The Interallied Memorial on the Cointe hill: a 75 m tower and a basilica raised in the 1930s by the WWI Allies to honour the 1914 defence of Liège — the lift up the tower gives the city's best panorama.

    Cointe, 4000 Liège, Belgium

    Recommended by Wikipedia, WBT

  49. Worth the detour · Liège

    Basilique Saint-Martin

    10th-c. collegiate church rebuilt in Gothic style (1506–42) on the aristocratic Mont-Saint-Martin — where the feast of Corpus Christi (Fête-Dieu) was first celebrated in 1246; 16th-c. stained glass and calvary.

    Mont-Saint-Martin, 4000 Liège, Belgium

    Recommended by Wikipedia, Visitliege

  50. Worth the detour · Liège

    Trinkhall Museum

    In the heart of Parc d'Avroy, a museum of ~3,000 works of 'situated art' made in workshops by artists with mental disabilities — one of the most original collections in Belgium.

    Parc d'Avroy, 4000 Liège, Belgium

    Recommended by Wikipedia, Visitliege

  51. Worth the detour · Liège

    Hôtel de Ville de Liège (La Violette)

    The 1714–18 town hall known as 'La Violette', its Louis XIV façade on the Place du Marché hiding a sumptuous interior of marble, stucco and grisailles.

    Place du Marché, 4000 Liège, Belgium

    Recommended by Wikipedia, Lonely Planet (FR edition)

  52. Worth the detour · Liège

    Parc d'Avroy

    Five-hectare landscape park in the city centre with a pond, statues and remarkable trees (a Cedar of Lebanon, bald cypresses, plane-tree alleys); the Trinkhall Museum sits in it.

    Avroy, 4000 Liège, Belgium

    Recommended by Le Guide du Routard (FR travel guide of record), Wikipedia

  53. Worth the detour · Liège

    Jardin botanique de Liège

    The University's former botanical garden (c. 3 ha), now a city park with some 400 trees including fifteen Belgian 'champion' specimens — sequoias, ginkgo, Japanese zelkova — and 19th-c. glasshouses.

    Centre, 4000 Liège, Belgium

    Recommended by Liegecity, Wikipedia

  54. Worth the detour · Liège

    En Roture (Outremeuse)

    Outremeuse's narrow restaurant lane — one cooking smell after another, small cafés and terraces, the nerve centre of the quarter's nightlife a step from the Meuse.

    En Roture, 4020 Liège, Belgium

    Recommended by Visitliege, Liegecity

  55. Worth the detour · Beer & Breweries · Liège

    Taverne Saint-Paul

    Old-world tavern a few steps from the cathedral, ranked #76 in The European Bar Guide's Top 100 European bars — a charming room from another era.

    Rue Saint-Paul 8, 4000 Liège, Belgium

    Recommended by Paris Match Belgique, Europeanbarguide

  56. Worth the detour · French & Brasserie · Liège

    Au Point de Vue

    Old-school brasserie looking onto the Opéra royal; its boulets won the Confrérie du Gay Boulet's Diamond Boulet in 2008.

    Place Verte 10, 4000 Liège, Belgium

    Recommended by Lonely Planet (FR edition), Wikipedia

  57. Worth the detour · Michelin & Fine Dining · Liège

    Au Moriane

    Michelin-selected and Gault&Millau-listed: Sébastien Lambert-Carabin's contemporary cooking of local produce in a monumentally renovated 17th-c. building on En Neuvice, near the Batte.

    En Neuvice 55, 4000 Liège, Belgium

    Recommended by Michelin, Gault&millau

  58. Worth the detour · Michelin & Fine Dining · Liège

    Grand Café de la Gare

    Gault&Millau-listed modern brasserie facing the Guillemins station — consistently high quality across a wide menu.

    Gare des Guillemins 20c, 4000 Liège, Belgium

    Recommended by Gault&millau, Moustique

  59. Worth the detour · Michelin & Fine Dining · Liège

    Baci

    Gault&Millau-listed restaurant inside the Théâtre de Liège — lively contemporary Mediterranean cooking that follows the seasons.

    Place du Vingt Août 16, 4000 Liège, Belgium

    Recommended by Gault&millau, Moustique

  60. Worth the detour · French & Brasserie · Liège

    Les Sabots d'Hélène

    Small bistro in the Carré on both Moustique's boulets list and sommelier Eric Boschman's nine best Liège restaurants.

    Rue Saint-Jean-en-Isle 18, 4000 Liège, Belgium

    Recommended by Moustique, Ericboschman

  61. Worth the detour · French & Brasserie · Liège

    Chez Philippe

    Boulets specialist near the Sauvenière — several house sauces and generous frites, simple wines.

    Rue Haute-Sauvenière 39, 4000 Liège, Belgium

    Recommended by Moustique, Gourmandiz

  62. Worth the detour · French & Brasserie · Liège

    La Mairie de Saint-Pholien

    Family-run Outremeuse table by Saint-Pholien serving Belgian and Liège classics, boulets included.

    Rue des Écoliers 16, 4020 Liège, Belgium

    Recommended by Moustique, Visitliege

  63. Worth the detour · Café & Brown Café · Liège

    Utamu Coffee'n Pastries

    Specialty coffee bar on Rue du Palais serving only East-African coffees with Belgian pastries given an African twist; named among Belgium's ten best specialty cafés in the European Coffee Trip awards.

    Rue du Palais 2, 4000 Liège, Belgium

    Recommended by Eurocoffeetrip, Elle Belgique (lifestyle/food editorial)

  64. Worth the detour · Michelin & Fine Dining · Liège

    Le Cabochon

    Michelin Bib Gourmand in Longdoz — a good-value, market-driven bistro menu across the river from the centre.

    Boulevard Émile de Laveleye 191, 4020 Liège, Belgium

    Recommended by Michelin

  65. Worth the detour · Michelin & Fine Dining · Liège

    Folies Gourmandes

    Gault&Millau-listed French restaurant on Rue des Clarisses near the Carré.

    Rue des Clarisses 48, 4000 Liège, Belgium

    Recommended by Gault&millau

  66. Worth the detour · Michelin & Fine Dining · Liège

    Walio

    Gault&Millau-listed: chef Vincenzo Calderone goes back to his Puglian and Sicilian roots with honest, full-flavoured cooking in the reconverted Val-Benoît.

    Val-Benoît, 4000 Liège, Belgium

    Recommended by Gault&millau

  67. Worth the detour · Michelin & Fine Dining · Liège

    La Cantina

    Gault&Millau-listed Italian restaurant by Saint-Denis, cooking for three decades.

    Rue Saint-Denis 2, 4000 Liège, Belgium

    Recommended by Gault&millau

  68. Worth the detour · Michelin & Fine Dining · Liège

    Les cinq étoiles

    Gault&Millau-listed Chinese restaurant on the Ourthe quays at Angleur.

    Quai des Ardennes 99, 4031 Angleur (Liège), Belgium

    Recommended by Gault&millau

  69. Worth the detour · Michelin & Fine Dining · Liège

    Sauvage

    Gault&Millau-listed: chef Hyun Frère's creative, refined cooking on the Route du Condroz.

    Route du Condroz 151, 4031 Angleur (Liège), Belgium

    Recommended by Gault&millau

  70. Deep cut · Liège

    Musée des Transports en commun de Wallonie

    Old Vennes tram depot full of Liège trams, trolleybuses and buses from horse-drawn days on — a nostalgic stop now the city's new tram is running again.

    Rue Richard Heintz 9, 4020 Liège, Belgium

    Recommended by ERIH, Visitliege, LA DH

  71. Deep cut · Liège

    Passerelle La Belle Liégeoise

    The 294 m footbridge (2016) linking Guillemins station to the Boverie park across the Meuse, named after the revolutionary feminist Théroigne de Méricourt.

    Passerelle La Belle Liégeoise, 4000 Liège, Belgium

    Recommended by Wikipedia, Lavenir, LA DH

  72. Deep cut · Café & Brown Café · Liège

    Constantin Café

    Small high-ceilinged coffee bar opened 2022 on Rue des Mineurs, styled like a brutalist antique shop by Volga's co-founder; pours Wide Awake (one of Belgium's best roasters) single origins.

    Rue des Mineurs 21, 4000 Liège, Belgium

    Recommended by Lefooding, Visitliege, Elle Belgique (lifestyle/food editorial)

  73. Deep cut · Liège

    Collégiale Sainte-Croix

    Notger's collegiate church of 979 with a rare Romanesque west choir — currently closed for a long restoration, but the building site opens for themed guided visits.

    Centre, 4000 Liège, Belgium

    Recommended by Wikipedia, Visitliege

  74. Deep cut · Liège

    Musée Grétry

    The Outremeuse birthplace of composer André-Modeste Grétry (1741), with his instruments, scores and period furnishings.

    Outremeuse, 4020 Liège, Belgium

    Recommended by Wikipedia, Visitliege

  75. Deep cut · Liège

    Le Forum

    Historic concert and comedy hall on Pont d'Avroy, one of Liège's main live-music venues.

    Rue Pont d'Avroy, 4000 Liège, Belgium

    Recommended by Wikipedia, Lonely Planet (FR edition)

  76. Deep cut · Michelin & Fine Dining · Liège

    Caudalie

    Michelin-selected contemporary French table run by sommelier Élodie Timmermans — the wine list is the point.

Around Liège 60

Spa & Francorchamps · Huy · the Meuse · Herve plateau · Val-Dieu · Blegny-Mine

  1. Must see · Beer & Breweries · Around Liège

    Abbaye du Val-Dieu

    The only abbey brewery still brewing inside its abbey walls in Wallonia's Pays de Herve — Val-Dieu ales poured in the abbey tavern; Saturday guided abbey + brewery tours with beer and Herve cheese.

    Val-Dieu, Aubel, Belgium

    Recommended by Official Site, WBT, RTBF (Belgian public broadcaster), Coe, Infolux

  2. Must see · Beer & Breweries · Around Liège

    Brasserie Grain d'Orge

    Family brewery at the Three Borders in Hombourg — Joup, Brice and the Aubel triple; pub with food Wed–Sun, cheese shop, and Saturday tours.

    Rue Laschet 3, 4852 Hombourg (Plombières), Belgium

    Recommended by Wikipedia, WBT, Lavenir, Moustique

  3. Must see · Around Liège

    Collégiale Notre-Dame de Huy

    Gothic collegiate church on the Meuse with the great rose window 'Li Rondia' and a treasury holding Mosan reliquary shrines of the 12th–13th c.

    Huy, Belgium

    Recommended by Lonely Planet (FR edition), Kikirpa, Wikipedia

  4. Must see · Around Liège

    Pouhon Pierre-le-Grand

    Victor Besme's 1880 octagonal pavilion over Spa's most famous iron-rich spring, named for Peter the Great who took the cure here in 1717 — taste the water, see the Livre d'Or painting of famous curistes.

    Spa, Belgium

    Recommended by Lonely Planet (FR edition), WBT, Wikipedia

  5. Must see · Around Liège

    Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps

    The 7 km Ardennes circuit of the Belgian Grand Prix since 1921 and its legendary Eau Rouge–Raidillon climb; tours, a museum in Stavelot abbey and race weekends all season.

    Route du Circuit, Francorchamps (Stavelot), Belgium

    Recommended by Wikipedia, Lonely Planet (FR edition), Official Site

  6. Must see · Around Liège

    Grottes de Remouchamps

    Show cave on the Amblève at Aywaille — a walk through vast chambers ending in what the caves bill as one of the longest underground boat rides in Europe.

    Remouchamps, Aywaille, Belgium

    Recommended by Wikipedia, Showcaves, RTBF (Belgian public broadcaster)

  7. Must see · Around Liège

    Château du Val-Saint-Lambert (Cristal Discovery)

    The former Cistercian abbey on the Meuse at Seraing where Val-Saint-Lambert has blown lead crystal since 1826 — the Cristal Discovery visit shows glassblowers at work and two centuries of pieces.

    Esplanade du Val, Seraing, Belgium

    Recommended by Lonely Planet (FR edition), WBT, Visitliege

  8. Must see · Around Liège

    Thermes de Spa

    The modern glass thermal baths on Annette-et-Lubin hill, reached by funicular from the town centre — naturally carbonated Spa waters in the town that gave every 'spa' its name, a UNESCO Great Spa Town of Europe since 2021.

    Colline d'Annette et Lubin, Spa, Belgium

    Recommended by WBT, Lonely Planet (FR edition), Lavenir

  9. Must see · Around Liège

    Abbaye de Stavelot

    The former prince-abbey of Stavelot-Malmedy, its 11th-c. church foundations laid open, now three museums: the Principality's history, Guillaume Apollinaire, and the Spa-Francorchamps circuit museum of F1 cars and bikes.

    Abbaye de Stavelot, Stavelot, Belgium

    Recommended by Official Site, Wikipedia, Lonely Planet (FR edition)

  10. Must see · Around Liège

    Fort de Loncin

    The most famous of Brialmont's ring of forts: on 15 Aug 1914 a German 'Big Bertha' shell blew up its magazine and entombed 350 defenders — the crater, the crypt-necropolis and a scenographic museum relive the moment.

    Fort de Loncin, Ans (Loncin), Belgium

    Recommended by Wikipedia, Visitliege, WBT

  11. Must see · Around Liège

    A 30-ha prehistory park around the Ramioul cave above the Meuse — hands-on flint-knapping, fire-making, reconstructed camps and a hunting trail; plan half a day.

    Rue de la Grotte 128, 4400 Flémalle, Belgium

    Recommended by RTBF (Belgian public broadcaster), Lavenir, WBT

  12. Must see · Around Liège

    Grand-Place, 4500 Huy, Belgium

    Recommended by Wikipedia, WBT, Le Guide du Routard (FR travel guide of record)

59 sights and 85 places to eat across Liège and the Meuse valley — from the 374 steps of the Montagne de Bueren, the Prince-Bishops' Palace, the Grand Curtius and La Boverie to the Sunday Batte market, Outremeuse and Calatrava's Guillemins station, out to Spa, Francorchamps, Huy, the abbey of Val-Dieu and the UNESCO coal mine at Blegny. A food canon all its own: boulets à la liégeoise in sauce lapin, the pearl-sugar gaufre de Liège, salade liégeoise, péket, sirop de Liège and Herve cheese.

How this guide was made

How the cuisine filters were policed

Every food card names a specific dish or beer — a label alone doesn’t qualify. The Liège canon: boulets à la liégeoise (sauce lapin with sirop de Liège), the pearl-sugar gaufre de Liège, salade liégeoise, péket, sirop de Liège and Herve cheese. Beer & breweries are their own grouped layer (Val-Dieu, Brasserie C, Jupiler’s Jupille). A cuisine tag names the kitchen’s own tradition, never one dish it happens to serve.

Web-searched in French and fact-checked

Every place is traceable to a credible source — Michelin, UNESCO, Gault&Millau, Le Soir, La Libre, RTBF, La Meuse, L’Avenir, Visit Liège, Wallonie Belgique Tourisme, beer authorities and vetted creators — recorded in data/sources.json. Every coordinate is verified into data/geocodes.json and every place status-checked. Yelp/TripAdvisor/RateBeer never count toward the two-source bar.
